Bunium bulbocastanum is a plant species in the family Apiaceae. 
It was once used as a root vegetable in parts of western Europe, and has been called great pignut or earthnut.

Growth
The plant is native to western Europe. It reaches about {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide, bearing frilly leaves and hermaphroditic flowers; it is pollinated by insects and self-fertile.{{citation needed|date=October 2013}}
The small, rounded taproot is edible raw or cooked, and said to taste like sweet chestnuts.{{citation needed|date=October 2013}} The leaf can be used as an herb or garnish similar to parsley.
